title: slo-degradation-empathy-script-qa-scratch-tomas
content:
Purpose / context:
- Scratchpad for a calm, empathetic internal comm when we surface a partial SLO degradation (latency or error spike) that could affect customer UX. Not for public comms — internal only (eng, product, cs, support leads).

TL;DR talking intent (for 1-min read):
- What happened: short, factual (what service affected, impact window estimate).
- What we're doing: clear immediate mitigation + who owns it.
- Short-term customer impact: honest, specific (which routes, what behavior).
- Next steps / when we'll update: timeline and channel.
- Tone: accountable, calm, non-defensive, focused on mitigation and runbook actions.

Primary audience segmentation (how to tailor):
- Support & CS leads: include reproducible conditions, affected customers list (if available), canned replies and escalation triggers.
- Product managers / PMM: include impact to features (chat API vs embedding), short term rollback/disable options, telemetry links.
- Engineers / SREs: include logs location, runbook step pointer, owner & pager, known hypotheses.
- Execs: high-level impact, customer/regulatory exposure, estimated end-to-end ROI on mitigations (if ask).

Tone guide (short snippets to borrow):
- Opening: "We’re seeing a partial degradation impacting inference latency for a subset of requests. Our SREs are investigating and we have mitigation X in flight."
- Empathy line for customer-facing teams: "We know this affects real product experiences and appreciate the patience as we work to restore normal performance."
- Accountability: "We’ll provide an update in 30–45 minutes, or sooner if the situation materially changes."
- Avoid definitive root-cause claims until RCA: "Early investigation points to X, but we are validating — we will not confirm a root cause until verified."

Suggested internal first message (channel: #ops-incident + email to relevant leads):
- Subject: [Incident] Partial SLO degradation — latency spike for text-generation routes
- Body bullets: 1) When noticed (time UTC) 2) Impacted surface (routes/model variants/regions) 3) Immediate mitigation (traffic routing, auto-scale bump, config rollback) 4) Owner (Pager, runbook link) 5) ETA for next update

Short FAQ / Q&A (prep answers so support & PMs can copy):
Q: Is user data at risk?
A: No indications of data loss or exfiltration. This is a performance degradation; security team is on standby and will escalate if anything changes.

Q: Which customers are affected?
A: At the moment, sampling shows elevated latency for requests hitting model XYZ in region eu-west-1 and for requests with prompt lengths > 1k tokens. We’ll share a customer list if we confirm tenant-level scope.

Q: Should we offer credits?
A: Not yet. Escalate to CS leadership for accounts asking for compensation; prepare precedent doc and timeline.

Q: Is a rollback possible?
A: Short-term mitigations are low-risk (route to smaller model variant / temporary drop-in caching). Full rollback of the model catalog is higher impact and requires PM/engineering signoff.

Quick canned replies (support copy/paste — internal):
- Short: "We’re aware of degraded performance for some requests and the team is actively working on a fix. We’ll update you within 45 minutes with more details."
- Mid: "We’re currently routing impacted traffic to a lower-latency model variant and monitoring. We do not believe customer data is affected. If you see persistent errors or can reproduce, please include request IDs and timestamps."

Runbook checklist (priority sequence):
1) Confirm signal: dashboards (latency p95/p99), error rate, CPU/GPU memory, autoscaler events.
2) Attach sample request IDs & logs to the incident (SRE-4829).
3) Attempt low-risk mitigation (reroute, cache warm, restrict large prompts), monitor.
4) Evaluate capacity: can we spin additional pods in region? If yes, do incremental scale.
5) If mitigations fail after 30m, escalate to product for feature gating / temporary disable.
6) Prepare internal post-incident comm template for later RCA.

Escalation triggers (to add to message):
- If p99 latency remains > 2x baseline after 30 minutes, escalate to on-call director.
- If any customer reports data integrity problems, escalate to security and legal immediately.
- If 3+ enterprise customers report SLA breaches, engage CRO / CS lead.

What we should not say (avoid these):
- "We think it's a bad model" (too early)
- "We're patching the infra" without clear owner
- Overpromising fix times

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Get a quick script for support to pull request IDs by time range (ask Rowan).
- Ask Legal: required phrasing if SLA threshold crossed (Anika).
- Shortlist customers likely to notice (top 20 revenue accounts) — prepare private comm if needed (Sahana to coordinate).
- Confirm if we should temporarily disable streaming on affected routes (product decision).

Pre-approved lines for exec updates (one-liners):
- "We identified elevated latency for a subset of requests; mitigations are in place and we expect resolution within the hour."
- "No customer data exposure identified. We will share an RCA within 48–72 hours."

Follow-ups / cadence:
- First internal update: at detection + 15–30 min (what we know now).
- Status update cadence: every 30–45 min until resolved.
- Post-incident: initial RCA draft within 48 hours; final RCA + remediation plan within 7 business days.

Notes to self (voice & ergonomics):
- Keep bullet-heavy messages; ops channels are noise-heavy — put the most critical facts first.
- Use timestamps (UTC) for reproducibility.
- Include runbook link and owner in every update so people can jump in without asking.
- If the incident spans >4 hours, schedule a brief async war-room summary for execs and CS.

Appendix: links to canned resources
- Incident comm templates: Confluence: incident-comm-templates (linked above)
- Runbooks: runbook/inference-degradation (ask infra-team for current location)
- Sample support reply repo: /contrib/support-canned-replies

Last pass checklist before posting initial message:
- [ ] Confirm owner (pager) is acknowledged
- [ ] Verify sample logs attached to incident ticket
- [ ] Legal/Privacy on standby if any data concerns are suspected
- [ ] CS has copy-paste replies and knows escalation path

—— end scratchpad ——

(If this gets used, need to trim and produce a single-slide quick-deck for execs and a 3-line pin for #company-status.)
